question: Who among the following has authored the play 'Nil Darpan'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dinabandhu Mitra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nil Darpan ("Mirror of Indigo") is a Bengali play written by Dinabandhu Mitra, first published in 1860. (नील दर्पण — दीनबंधु मित्र)

 

• The play depicts the brutal exploitation of indigo cultivators (ryots) by British indigo planters in Bengal during the Indigo Revolt (Neel Bidroha) of 1859-60.

 

• Its English translation, titled 'Nil Darpan or The Indigo Planting Mirror', was published by Reverend James Long, who was later prosecuted and fined for it; Michael Madhusudan Dutt anonymously assisted with the translation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dinabandhu Mitra was later honoured with the title 'Rai Bahadur' by the British government for his services as a postal inspector, despite writing this anti-planter play.

 

NOTE

 

• Motilal Nehru (Option 1): A prominent lawyer and Congress leader, father of Jawaharlal Nehru, and co-founder of the Swaraj Party.

 

• Chittaranjan Das (Option 2): Popularly known as Deshbandhu, he co-founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 with Motilal Nehru.

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 4): Known as the 'Nightingale of India' (Bharat Kokila), the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (1925) and first woman Governor of an Indian state (UP).

question: Which of the following awards was won by Lata Mangeshkar in the year 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Ratna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 2001. (भारत रत्न — लता मंगेशकर)

 

• She was only the second playback singer to receive the Bharat Ratna, after M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998), and remains one of the very few musicians to receive this honour.

 

• Lata Mangeshkar, known as the 'Nightingale of India' / 'Queen of Melody', sang in over 36 languages across a career spanning more than seven decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• She had already received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1989 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1999, before being conferred the Bharat Ratna.

 

• She passed away on 6 February 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award (Option 1): She received this in 1993; it is a film-industry award, not a national civilian honour.

 

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 2): India's second-highest civilian award, conferred on her in 1999, before the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Dadasaheb Phalke Award (Option 3): India's highest award in cinema, conferred on her in 1989, well before 2001.

question: Which of the following is a correct order of basicity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CsOH>KOH>NaOH>LiOH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Basicity (base strength) of alkali metal hydroxides increases down Group 1 of the periodic table, from Li to Cs. (क्षारीयता — CsOH सबसे प्रबल क्षार)

 

• As we move down the group, atomic/ionic size increases, which decreases the lattice energy and increases ionic character of the M-OH bond, making the hydroxide ion easier to release. This makes the hydroxide a stronger base.

 

• Hence, in decreasing order of basicity: CsOH > KOH > NaOH > LiOH, the exact reverse of increasing atomic number.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same trend of increasing basic character down a group applies to alkaline earth metal hydroxides too, e.g., Mg(OH)2 < Ca(OH)2 < Sr(OH)2 < Ba(OH)2.

 

• LiOH is the weakest base among alkali metal hydroxides and, unlike the others, decomposes on heating to give Li2O, showing its diagonal relationship with Mg.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (LiOH>NaOH>KOH>CsOH): This is the exact reverse of the correct trend.

 

• Option 2 (LiOH>KOH>CsOH>NaOH): Incorrectly places LiOH, the weakest base, first, and disorders the remaining three.

 

• Option 3 (KOH>CsOH>NaOH>LiOH): Incorrectly places KOH above CsOH.

question: Who founded the Prarthana Samaj in Mumbai in 1867?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atmaram Pandurang.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1867 by Dr. Atmaram Pandurang, with associates such as Dr. R.G. Bhandarkar and M.G. Ranade joining and strengthening it later. (प्रार्थना समाज — आत्माराम पांडुरंग)

 

• It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and worked for social reform — monotheism, opposition to caste distinctions, widow remarriage, and women's education — while retaining more Hindu ritual elements than the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Under Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade, the Prarthana Samaj's social reform activities expanded significantly, including efforts for widow remarriage and the spread of education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Associated reformer Justice Ranade also helped establish the Social Conference, an offshoot of the Indian National Congress focused on social reform.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Option 2): A moderate Congress leader who founded the Servants of India Society in 1905; associated with, but did not found, the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Shri Ram Bajpai (Option 3): Not associated with founding the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy (Option 4): Founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta in 1828, the movement that inspired the Prarthana Samaj but is a distinct organisation.

question: Who among the following formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) was formed in 1929 by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati to mobilise peasants against the exploitative zamindari system. (किसान सभा — स्वामी सहजानंद सरस्वती)

 

• This became the foundation for the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), formed in 1936 at Lucknow, with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as its first President.

 

• He is regarded as the 'Father of the Kisan Movement' in India, and organised major peasant struggles in Bihar such as the Bakasht land movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The All India Kisan Sabha's journal was called 'Hunkar', and its well-known slogan was 'Land to the tiller'.

 

NOTE

 

• Kunwar Singh (Option 1): A veteran leader of the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar (Jagdishpur), unrelated to the 1929 Kisan Sabha.

 

• JM Sengupta (Option 2): A Congress leader and Mayor of Calcutta, associated with Bengal politics, not the Bihar Kisan Sabha.

 

• Jayprakash Narayan (Option 3): A prominent socialist leader who later worked with the peasant movement in Bihar, but did not form the BPKS in 1929.

question: In which city was the first golf club of India situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Royal Calcutta Golf Club, established in Kolkata in 1829, is the first golf club in India and the oldest golf club outside the United Kingdom. (रॉयल कलकत्ता गोल्फ क्लब — कोलकाता, 1829)

 

• It received the prefix 'Royal' from King Edward VII in 1911, becoming one of the few clubs in the world with royal patronage from outside Britain.

 

• It is also recognised as the oldest golf club in Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Naldehra Golf Course in Shimla, established in 1905 by Lord Curzon, is one of the oldest golf courses in India but not the first golf club.

 

• The Gulmarg Golf Club in Jammu & Kashmir is famous for having the highest green golf course in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Shimla (Option 1): Home to the historic Naldehra Golf Club (1905), but not the first in India.

 

• Gulmarg (Option 2): Known for its high-altitude golf course, established later than Calcutta's.

 

• Mysore (Option 3): Has a well-known golf club but not the country's first.

question: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 226.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari — for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose, making its scope wider than Article 32. (अनुच्छेद 226 — उच्च न्यायालय की रिट क्षेत्राधिकार)

 

• Article 32, called the 'heart and soul of the Constitution' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, gives the Supreme Court the power to issue the same writs, but only for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

 

• Thus Article 226 is the High Court's counterpart to Article 32, though the High Court's writ jurisdiction is concurrent with, and broader than, that of the Supreme Court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 32 itself is also a Fundamental Right, so it cannot be suspended except during a National Emergency (Article 359), whereas Article 226 is not a Fundamental Right.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 227 (Option 1): Gives High Courts the power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals within their territorial jurisdiction.

 

• Article 228 (Option 2): Allows a High Court to withdraw a case from a subordinate court if it involves a substantial question of constitutional law.

 

• Article 225 (Option 3): Deals with the jurisdiction of existing High Courts continuing under the Constitution.

question: Mahendravarman I was the ruler of which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pallava.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahendravarman I (c. 600-630 CE) was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram. (महेन्द्रवर्मन प्रथम — पल्लव वंश)

 

• He was a great patron of art and architecture, credited with starting the tradition of rock-cut cave temples in South India, and held the title 'Vichitrachitta' (curious-minded).

 

• He was also a playwright, and authored the Sanskrit satirical play 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• His son Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) defeated the Chalukyan king Pulakeshin II and built the famous rathas at Mahabalipuram.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandya (Option 1): A Tamil dynasty centred at Madurai, contemporaneous rivals of the Pallavas and Cholas.

 

• Chola (Option 2): A major South Indian dynasty, later famous under rulers like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, distinct from the Pallavas.

 

• Chalukya (Option 3): The Chalukyas of Badami, under Pulakeshin II, were the chief rivals of the Pallavas in the Deccan.

question: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inconsistent regulatory environment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A frequently cited challenge for foreign investment (FDI) in India is an inconsistent/complex regulatory environment — frequent policy changes, multiple approval layers, and differing state-level rules — which creates uncertainty for foreign investors. (विदेशी निवेश — नियामकीय अस्थिरता)

 

• This includes issues such as retrospective taxation, land acquisition hurdles, and bureaucratic delays, historically flagged in Ease of Doing Business assessments.

 

• The Government of India has taken steps such as liberalising FDI limits, single-window clearance systems, and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to address such concerns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India steadily improved its World Bank Ease of Doing Business ranking in past years partly by addressing regulatory bottlenecks (the index itself was discontinued by the World Bank in 2021).

 

• FDI inflows into India are tracked by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

 

NOTE

 

• Excessive foreign competition (Option 1): Not typically identified as a barrier to *inbound* foreign investment; more relevant to domestic industry protection debates.

 

• Lack of skilled labour (Option 3): India has a large working-age population, so this is not generally cited as the primary challenge for FDI.

 

• Lack of consumer base (Option 4): India's large and growing consumer market is in fact one of its key attractions for foreign investors, not a challenge.

question: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jitendra Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Jitendra Singh has served as the Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences since 2021, and continued in this role as of July 2023. (डॉ. जितेंद्र सिंह — विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्री)

 

• He also holds charge of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (MoS, Independent Charge), and the Department of Space and Atomic Energy (as Minister of State in the PMO).

 

• He represents the Udhampur constituency in Jammu & Kashmir.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under his tenure, initiatives such as the National Research Foundation (NRF) and the VAIBHAV Fellowship for overseas Indian scientists were launched.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramesh Pokhriyal (Option 1): Former Union Minister of Human Resource Development / Education, not Science and Technology.

 

• Dharmendra Pradhan (Option 2): Union Minister of Education and Skill Development, not Science and Technology.

 

• Ashwini Vaishnaw (Option 3): Union Minister for Railways, Communications and Electronics & IT, not Science and Technology.

question: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lathmar Holi is celebrated primarily in the twin towns of Barsana and Nandgaon in the Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh. (लठमार होली — बरसाना, उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• In this unique tradition, women of Barsana (Radha's legendary birthplace) playfully beat men from Nandgaon (Krishna's village) with wooden sticks (lathis), while the men defend themselves with shields.

 

• It commemorates the legend of Lord Krishna visiting Radha's village Barsana to play Holi, where he was playfully driven away by the women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other unique regional forms of Holi in India include Hola Mohalla (Punjab, Sikh martial tradition) and Phoolon wali Holi (Vrindavan, played with flowers).

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Not associated with Lathmar Holi; celebrates its own regional festivals like Ugadi.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 2): Known for festivals like Losar and Solung, not Lathmar Holi.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Known for festivals like Kullu Dussehra, not Lathmar Holi.

question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President's office in India?
option_1: He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.
option_2: He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.
option_3: The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
option_4: He shall not hold any office of profit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 59 of the Constitution, which lays down the conditions of the President's office, the President is actually entitled to the use of his official residences (Rashtrapati Bhavan) without payment of rent — the statement reverses this, so it is NOT a genuine condition. (अनुच्छेद 59 — राष्ट्रपति पद की शर्तें)

 

• The genuine conditions under Article 59 include: the President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a State Legislature; shall not hold any other office of profit; is entitled to use official residences without payment of rent; and his emoluments and allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.

 

• These provisions exist to ensure the independence and dignity of the President's office.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The President's emoluments, allowances and privileges are determined by Parliament by law and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Correctly reflects Article 59 — the President must vacate any seat in Parliament or a State Legislature upon assuming office.

 

• Option 3: Correctly reflects Article 59 — the President's allowances cannot be reduced during the term, protecting the office from legislative pressure.

 

• Option 4: Correctly reflects Article 59 — the President cannot hold any other office of profit while in office.

question: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine's list of '100 most influential people of 2021'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narendra Modi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi was featured in Time Magazine's list of the '100 Most Influential People of 2021', published in September 2021. (टाइम पत्रिका 100 प्रभावशाली लोग — नरेंद्र मोदी)

 

• The 2021 list also included two other Indians: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Serum Institute of India CEO Adar Poonawalla.

 

• Time's profile of PM Modi in this list, written by comedian Ronny Chieng, was critical in tone regarding India's handling of the COVID-19 second wave, and generated controversy in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra later featured in Time's other lists (such as 'Next Generation Leaders') following his Tokyo Olympics gold medal (August 2021), but not in the main 2021 'Time 100' list, which was published before the Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• Neeraj Chopra (Option 1): India's Olympic javelin throw gold medallist (Tokyo 2020/2021); not on the 2021 Time 100 main list.

 

• Virat Kohli (Option 3): Star Indian cricketer; not featured on the 2021 Time 100 list.

 

• Amit Shah (Option 4): Union Home Minister of India; not featured on the 2021 Time 100 list.

question: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Physiological density.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Physiological density is calculated as the total population of a region divided by its net cultivated (arable) land area, rather than the total geographical area. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — कृषि योग्य भूमि पर आधारित भौतिकीय घनत्व)

 

• It reflects the pressure of population on agricultural land and is a more meaningful indicator of land-population pressure than simple (arithmetic) density.

 

• A higher physiological density indicates that the available cultivated land must support a larger number of people, implying greater strain on agricultural resources.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arithmetic (crude) density = total population ÷ total land area of a region.

 

• Agricultural density = total agricultural population (cultivators + agricultural labourers) ÷ net cultivable area — a related but distinct measure that uses only the farming population, not the total population.

 

NOTE

 

• Agricultural density (Option 1): Uses the agricultural population, not the total population, in the numerator — a different measure.

 

• Gross density (Option 3): Another name for arithmetic density, calculated using total geographical area, not net cultivated area.

 

• Net density (Option 4): Not a standard term for this specific measure; it does not correspond to the net-cultivated-area-based calculation described.

question: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the ____________ Award in the year 1994.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grammy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, the inventor of the Mohan Veena, won the Grammy Award for Best World Music Album in 1994 for the album 'A Meeting by the River', recorded with American slide guitarist Ry Cooder. (ग्रैमी पुरस्कार — विश्व मोहन भट्ट)

 

• The Mohan Veena is a modified Indian slide guitar/veena hybrid instrument that he developed himself.

 

• He was the first Indian to win a Grammy Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vishwa Mohan Bhatt was also honoured with the Padma Shri (2002) and Padma Bhushan (2017) by the Government of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangita Kalanidhi (Option 1): A prestigious title conferred by the Madras Music Academy, not what he won in 1994.

 

• Oscar (Option 2): An American Academy Award for films; unrelated to this music honour.

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi (Option 4): India's national academy for music, dance and drama, a separate award from the Grammy.

question: Which plateaus are very fertile because they are rich in black soil that is very good for farming?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deccan lava plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deccan lava plateau (Deccan Traps) of peninsular India is composed of basaltic lava rock, which weathers to form the extremely fertile black soil (regur soil), ideal for cotton cultivation. (दक्कन लावा पठार — काली मिट्टी)

 

• This soil is also known as 'black cotton soil' because of its wide use for growing cotton across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.

 

• Black soil has high clay content, retains moisture well, and is rich in iron, magnesium and lime, though relatively poor in nitrogen and phosphorus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Traps were formed by intense volcanic activity around 66 million years ago, near the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary, and are among the largest volcanic provinces on Earth.

 

NOTE

 

• African plateau (Option 1): A general term for the plateau region of the African continent, not specifically known for black soil.

 

• Ethiopian plateau (Option 2): Known for its high elevation and volcanic origin, but not specifically famed for black cotton soil in the same sense.

 

• Katanga plateau (Option 3): Located in the Democratic Republic of Congo, notable for copper and cobalt mineral deposits, not agricultural black soil.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tissue-organ grade organisation - Euplectella.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Euplectella (Venus's flower basket) is a sponge (phylum Porifera), which exhibits cellular grade of organisation, not tissue-organ grade — making this pairing incorrect. (यूप्लेक्टेला — कोशिकीय स्तर संगठन, स्पंज)

 

• In cellular grade organisation (seen in Porifera, e.g., Sycon, Euplectella, Spongilla), cells show division of labour but are not organised into true tissues.

 

• Tissue-organ grade organisation is seen in flatworms (Platyhelminthes, e.g., Planaria), where cells are organised into tissues that further form organs, but no true organ-systems exist yet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The complete hierarchy of grades of organisation is: Protoplasmic grade → Cellular grade → Cell-tissue grade → Tissue-organ grade → Organ-system grade, representing increasing levels of complexity in the animal kingdom.

 

• Organ-system grade organisation is found in higher animals such as Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, and Chordata, where organs work together in coordinated systems.

 

NOTE

 

• Cellular grade organisation - Sycon (Option 1): Correct pairing; Sycon is a sponge (Porifera) showing cellular grade organisation.

 

• Protoplasmic grade organisation - Paramecium (Option 2): Correct pairing; in Protozoans like Paramecium, all life activities are carried out by a single cell (or its organelles).

 

• Cell-tissue grade organisation - Jellyfish (Option 3): Correct pairing; Coelenterates (Cnidaria) such as jellyfish show cells organised into definite tissues.

question: Who is the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu as of July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MK Stalin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M.K. Stalin, leader of the DMK (Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam), has been the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu since 7 May 2021, and continued in this position as of July 2023. (एम.के. स्टालिन — तमिलनाडु के मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He is the son of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK stalwart M. Karunanidhi.

 

• He represents the Kolathur constituency in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamil Nadu's capital is Chennai; the state has previously been led by iconic Chief Ministers including C.N. Annadurai, M.G. Ramachandran, and J. Jayalalithaa.

 

NOTE

 

• Pinarayi Vijayan (Option 1): Chief Minister of Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

 

• M Yedurappa (Option 2): Former Chief Minister of Karnataka, from the BJP.

 

• KN Nehru (Option 3): A Tamil Nadu cabinet minister (Municipal Administration), not the Chief Minister.

question: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhya Pradesh is the largest producer of pulses in India, contributing roughly a fifth or more of the country's total pulses production. (दलहन उत्पादन में अग्रणी राज्य — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The state is a major grower of chana (gram/chickpea), India's most widely cultivated pulse crop, along with tur (arhar) and other pulses.

 

• Other leading pulses-producing states include Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India is the world's largest producer as well as consumer of pulses, though it also imports pulses to meet domestic demand.

 

• The Government of India promotes pulses cultivation under schemes like the National Food Security Mission (NFSM) – Pulses.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 2): A leading producer of wheat and rice, not among the top pulses-producing states.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Known primarily for wheat and rice cultivation under the Green Revolution, not a leading pulses producer.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Produces some pulses but ranks well below Madhya Pradesh in total pulses output.

question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1973.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Project Tiger was launched by the Government of India on 1 April 1973 at Corbett National Park, Uttarakhand (then Uttar Pradesh), to conserve the declining tiger population. (प्रोजेक्ट टाइगर — 1973)

 

• It began with 9 tiger reserves; India now has over 50 tiger reserves under Project Tiger.

 

• The project is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), established in 2005.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India celebrated the 50th anniversary of Project Tiger in 2023; the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) was also launched by PM Modi in April 2023 at this milestone event.

 

NOTE

 

• 1985 (Option 1): Not associated with Project Tiger's launch.

 

• 1972 (Option 3): The year the Wildlife Protection Act was enacted, providing the legal framework, but Project Tiger itself was launched the following year, in 1973.

 

• 1970 (Option 4): The year India imposed a ban on tiger hunting, a precursor step, but Project Tiger was launched in 1973.

question: The head office of Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), the governing body for cricket in India, has its headquarters in Mumbai, Maharashtra. (बीसीसीआई मुख्यालय — मुंबई)

 

• BCCI is registered as a society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, with its headquarters located at the Cricket Centre, Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.

 

• It is the richest cricket board in the world and organises major domestic tournaments such as the Ranji Trophy and the Indian Premier League (IPL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• BCCI is affiliated to the International Cricket Council (ICC), whose headquarters is in Dubai, UAE.

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkata (Option 2): Home to the historic Eden Gardens stadium, but not the BCCI headquarters.

 

• New Delhi (Option 3): Seat of the Indian government, not the BCCI's headquarters.

 

• Chennai (Option 4): Home ground of Tamil Nadu cricket and the Chepauk stadium, but not the BCCI headquarters.

question: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decomposition of calcium carbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Calcium carbonate decomposes on heating as: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. This is a thermal decomposition reaction, but not a redox reaction, because the oxidation states of Ca (+2), C (+4) and O (-2) remain unchanged on both sides. (अपघटन अभिक्रिया — कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट, गैर-रेडॉक्स)

 

• A reaction is classified as redox only if there is a change in oxidation number of at least one element, involving simultaneous oxidation and reduction.

 

• In contrast, decomposition of water (2H2O → 2H2 + O2), sodium hydride (2NaH → 2Na + H2), and potassium chlorate (2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2) all involve a change in oxidation states, making them redox reactions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Decomposition reactions that do NOT involve a change in oxidation state (like carbonates and some hydrates breaking down) are examples of non-redox decomposition, common among metal carbonates and bicarbonates on heating.

 

NOTE

 

• Decomposition of dihydrogen monoxide, i.e. water (Option 1): Hydrogen changes from +1 to 0 and oxygen from -2 to 0 — a redox reaction.

 

• Decomposition of sodium hydride (Option 2): Hydrogen changes from -1 (in NaH) to 0 (H2) — a redox reaction.

 

• Decomposition of potassium chlorate (Option 3): Chlorine changes from +5 to -1, and oxygen from -2 to 0 — a redox reaction.

question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?
option_1: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium
solution_text:
The correct answer is A flower with both androecium and gynoecium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Monoecious plants bear both the male reproductive part (androecium) and the female reproductive part (gynoecium), whether combined in bisexual flowers or as separate unisexual male and female flowers, on the same individual plant. (एकलिंगाश्रयी/उभयलिंगाश्रयी — नर व मादा दोनों अंग एक ही पौधे पर)

 

• Common examples of monoecious plants include maize, cucumber, coconut, and castor, where the same plant bears both types of reproductive structures.

 

• This is contrasted with dioecious plants (e.g., papaya, date palm, mulberry), where male and female flowers occur on separate individual plants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A flower possessing both androecium and gynoecium in the same flower is termed a bisexual (hermaphrodite) flower; a flower with only one of the two is a unisexual (male or female) flower.

 

• The presence of both reproductive whorls (male and female) within the same plant, whether in one flower or in separate flowers, is what defines the plant as monoecious.

 

NOTE

 

• A flower with dithecous (Option 2): 'Dithecous' describes an anther with two thecae (lobes), a feature of stamen structure — unrelated to the monoecious/dioecious classification.

 

• A flower with gynoecium only (Option 3): Describes a unisexual female (pistillate) flower, which alone does not define a monoecious plant.

 

• A flower with androecium only (Option 4): Describes a unisexual male (staminate) flower, which alone does not define a monoecious plant.

question: ___________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Microfinance Institutions Network.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is a Reserve Bank of India (RBI)-recognised Self-Regulatory Organisation (SRO) for the microfinance industry, working towards the sector's orderly and robust growth. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस संस्थान नेटवर्क — MFIN)

 

• MFIN was established in 2009 and works towards responsible lending, client protection, and policy advocacy for NBFC-MFIs (Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions).

 

• It maintains a credit bureau data-sharing system among its member microfinance institutions to prevent over-indebtedness of borrowers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sa-Dhan is another RBI-recognised SRO for the microfinance sector in India, alongside MFIN.

 

NOTE

 

• Self-help Group Association (Option 1): Not a recognised industry SRO for microfinance; SHGs are grassroots community savings/credit groups.

 

• Microfinance and Investments Regulatory Authority (Option 3): Not an actual RBI-recognised body; a distractor name.

 

• NABARD (Option 4): The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development is an apex development finance institution, not an industry self-regulatory organisation for microfinance.

question: Details about Sudarshana lake is given in a rock inscription at Girnar (Junagarh), which was composed to record the achievements of the Shaka ruler _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rudradaman I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription, dated to around 150 CE, was composed to record the achievements of the Western Kshatrapa (Shaka) ruler Rudradaman I, and famously describes the repair of the Sudarshana lake. (जूनागढ़ शिलालेख — रुद्रदामन प्रथम)

 

• This inscription is historically significant as it is the earliest known major inscription written in chaste/classical Sanskrit, unlike the earlier Ashokan edicts, which were largely in Prakrit.

 

• Sudarshana Lake, near Girnar in present-day Gujarat, was originally built during the Mauryan period under Chandragupta Maurya's governor Pushyagupta, and later repaired by Rudradaman I after a devastating storm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same Sudarshana Lake dam was repaired again later by Skandagupta's governor Parnadatta, as recorded in a separate Junagadh inscription of the Gupta period.

 

• Rudradaman I belonged to the Western Kshatrapas (Shaka Kshatrapas) dynasty, ruling over parts of western and central India.

 

NOTE

 

• Rudrasimha III (Option 1): The last ruler of the Western Kshatrapa dynasty, defeated by Gupta emperor Chandragupta II; not linked to this inscription.

 

• Chashtana (Option 3): Founder of the Western Kshatrapa (Shaka) dynasty at Ujjain, and grandfather of Rudradaman I, but not the ruler credited in this inscription.

 

• Maues (Option 4): An early Indo-Scythian (Saka) king who ruled in the northwest (Gandhara region), unrelated to the Junagadh/Girnar inscription.
